cards.text: It's the heat of the day by the Oaks of Mamre, the kind of heat where nobody moves unless they have to. Abraham, the man God promised would be the father of many nations (Gen 17:5), is sitting at the entrance of his tent. Then the LORD appears to him.

cards.question: Abraham looks up from the entrance of his tent. He sees ___ men standing nearby.
Remember, it's the heat of the day. True or false: when Abraham sees the men, he runs from his tent to meet them.

cards.text: Hottest part of the day, and this man RUNS out there like he just heard the oven timer go off. He bows low to the ground, says, "My lord," and begs them not to pass him by.

cards.question: Abraham wants the three men to stop and rest under the tree. What does he offer them first?

answers.text: Robes to wear in the shade

cards.question: Abraham also promises a bit of ___ so the men can refresh themselves before they go on their way.

cards.text: They say yes, and Abraham hurries into the tent to his wife Sarah: "Quick! Prepare three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread." A BIT of bread, he said, which is like me promising you one cookie and then firing up EVERY oven in the Dorinverse.

cards.question: Meanwhile, Abraham runs off to find something special for the meal. What does he pick out for his three guests?

answers.text: A young goat from the flock

cards.question: A servant hurries to prepare the calf, and Abraham sets it in front of the men under the tree, along with curds and milk. True or false: Abraham sits down and eats with them.
The men are eating, and Abraham is standing by them under the tree. Then they ask him something. What do they ask?

cards.text: "There, in the tent," Abraham says, and notice they asked for Sarah by name. I bet Abraham feels like he just got a text from a number he doesn't have saved, asking how his wife is doing.

cards.question: Then the LORD speaks to Abraham. True or false: the LORD says that at this time next year, Sarah will have a son.

cards.text: Now Sarah is behind him at the entrance to the tent, listening. And Abraham and Sarah are already old, and Sarah has passed the age of childbearing.

cards.question: Sarah is old and past childbearing, and she just heard she'll have a son. She ___ to herself.

cards.text: She says to herself, "After I am worn out and my master is old, will I now have this pleasure?" A quiet little laugh, like when you giggle on mute during a work call and you're SURE nobody heard.

cards.question: Sarah laughed to herself. Then the ___ asks Abraham why Sarah laughed.
Sarah wondered whether she could really bear a child when she's old. The LORD answers with a question of His own. What's His point?

answers.text: Nothing is too difficult for the LORD
Sarah should not listen at the tent
Abraham should have told her sooner

cards.question: The LORD says it again: in about a year, Sarah will have a son. But Sarah is afraid. What does she say?
Sarah says, "I did not laugh." True or false: the LORD answers that she did laugh.

cards.text: I've said "What dough?" with dough still on my mustache, friend, so no judging from me. We'll stop here for now, but this story is a long way from done.
